mechanism_narrative: A month-over-month decline in the federal funds rate signals an accommodative monetary policy stance that reduces discount rates for equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS declines, or Rank IC falls below 0.02 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 4.5%, it indicates restrictive monetary policy that increases borrowing costs and dampens corporate earnings growth, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS > 4.5%, or Rank IC remains below 0.02 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in federal funds rate and decline in non-farm payrolls signals monetary tightening coinciding with labor market weakness, creating dual headwinds for corporate earnings that drive negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: The joint signal (FEDFUNDS rising and PAYEMS declining) fails to predict negative returns in >55% of cases, or interaction term Rank IC < 0.02 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansions, residential construction permits (HOUST) exceeding 1800 thousand units signal robust housing demand that supports consumer spending and corporate profits, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: In late-cycle expansions, SPX 60-day returns are positive in <45% of HOUST > 1800 periods, or Rank IC < 0.02 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: A month-over-month increase in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) indicates strengthening labor market conditions that boost consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in >55% of PAYEMS increase periods, or Rank IC < 0.02 over 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate falls below 4.5%, it signals a tight labor market that may trigger inflationary pressures and subsequent monetary tightening, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 5 days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in >55% of UNRATE < 4.5% periods, or Rank IC < 0.02 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in consumer spending (RSAFS) and industrial production (INDPRO) signals broad-based economic strength that supports corporate earnings growth, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: The joint signal (RSAFS rising and INDPRO rising) fails to predict positive returns in >55% of cases, or interaction term Rank IC < 0.02 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: In post-recession recoveries, industrial production (INDPRO) exceeding 110 index points signals improving manufacturing capacity utilization that boosts corporate profits, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: In post-recession recoveries, SPX 60-day returns are positive in <45% of INDPRO > 110 periods, or Rank IC < 0.02 over 3-year windows.
